11.4b — MC Practice 2: Data & Networks

Target practice. Set 2 drills the data families (DAT-1, DAT-2, AAP-1 — binary, lists, filtering) and the network families (CSN-1, CSN-2 — packets, routing, redundancy). These are the questions your 9.1a–9.9a units mapped directly, so today is verification: do you score what you learned?

Warm Drill ~10 min

Round the bases, 90 seconds each — write answers, then check neighbors:

  1. (DAT-1) A list of 32 student names — minimum bits to give each a unique ID? (2⁵ = 32 → 5 bits)
  2. (DAT-2) The dataset column "rating 1–5" — which operation answers "most common rating"? (a tally per value — the MODE — how would you loop it in pseudocode?)
  3. (CSN-1) Why can the internet "route around damage"? (no single path — packets re-route; a router is a local decision, not a map)
  4. (CSN-2) Why is UDP right for game packets and TCP right for the game's download? (9.8a — drop vs. wait)
Practice Set 2 ~35 min

18 questions, 18 minutes, timed. Heavier weight on your Set 1 error-table families. Then the scorecard ritual again:

  1. Grade → error table v2 (family / time / right-wrong)
  2. Compare to Set 1: did the weak family improve? If not — WHY not (misconception, not speed: wrong tells you what to re-read)
  3. The misconception hunt: for each wrong answer, write the sentence of what you BELIEVED. "The mode is the average" is a fixable sentence; "I guessed C" is not.

Pair-teach (10 min): find someone whose error table is strong where yours is weak. They explain their attack on 2 questions; you explain yours. Teaching is the fastest known study method — this is 1.1a's pair setup running one last time.

Bug Hunt: Misconception museum

  1. "Lossless compression makes files smaller without any tradeoff." What is the tradeoff the exam wants named (compression time / complexity — 9.3a)?
  2. "HTTPS means the site is safe to buy from." What does TLS ACTUALLY guarantee vs not guarantee (private line; NOT legitimacy — 9.9a)?
  3. "Removing a filter makes data more accurate." Which way does filtering trade — and what did 9.6a say about scope (cleaner AND less representative — both true)?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Score Set 2 with a family-labeled error table
  • Write the misconception sentence for every miss
  • Teach one question to someone whose table is weak there
  • Know which families you'll drill before 11.4c
